title: Compliance Advisory & Governance
metaDescription: Governance and compliance advisory that keeps a cybersecurity program demonstrably aligned to the regulatory framework it operates under, over time.
heroDek: A program that was compliant at the last audit and a program that is compliant today are not automatically the same program. Governance is what keeps the two in sync.
contextHeading: Compliant and defensible are related, not identical
contextParagraphs: A cybersecurity program can pass an audit and still be poorly governed — controls implemented to satisfy a specific finding, with no process behind them for staying current as systems, personnel, and the regulatory framework itself change. That gap tends to surface at the worst time: the next audit cycle, or an incident that reveals a control existed on paper but not in practice.

GSS builds governance structures that keep pace with the program rather than trailing it: clear ownership for each control, documentation that reflects the system as it actually operates, and a review cadence that catches drift before a regulator does. For nuclear and adjacent critical-infrastructure environments, that means governance built by people who have sat on the regulator's side of the table — the cyber-physical division includes former U.S. NRC inspectors who authored the cybersecurity regulations now governing U.S. plants, so the advisory reflects what a review will actually test for.

This work is distinct from a one-time compliance assessment. It's the ongoing structure — policy, roles, documentation, and reporting — that makes a program's compliant status something the organization can demonstrate on any given day, not just reconstruct under pressure before an audit.

methodology.label: Framework Mapping
methodology.body: Applicable regulatory and standards requirements mapped against the program's current state.

methodology.label: Governance Structure Design
methodology.body: Roles, ownership, and decision authority defined for each control area.

methodology.label: Policy & Documentation
methodology.body: Policies and evidence brought into alignment with how systems actually operate.

methodology.label: Gap Remediation Planning
methodology.body: Deviations from the framework prioritized and assigned for correction.

methodology.label: Audit & Review Readiness
methodology.body: Documentation packaged for regulator, licensee, or third-party review.

methodology.label: Ongoing Governance
methodology.body: Review cadence established to keep the program aligned as it evolves.

faq.q: Is this a one-time compliance assessment or an ongoing service?
faq.a: Both are available, but the governance structure itself is designed to operate on an ongoing basis so alignment doesn't lapse between reviews.

faq.q: Does the team have direct regulatory-inspection experience?
faq.a: Yes — the cyber-physical division includes former U.S. NRC inspectors who authored the cybersecurity regulations now governing U.S. plants.

faq.q: How does this relate to the physical-security regulatory compliance capability?
faq.a: They're coordinated. Physical security compliance and cybersecurity compliance are handled as related but distinct workstreams, reflecting how most regulatory frameworks actually treat them.
